questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture of the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. It was not very intuitive, but the mobility offices were quick to answer emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an intro day at the university, where we got some information. The university also sent us a book about the Erasmus programme before we arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very hard to find housing. The university was not of any help even though they said they could help us find housing. I would recommend writing to the university as soon as you get accepted.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the distance. The public transportation is quite bad. I would recommend to live in walking distance from Campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to register for courses online in June and then you got your answer about three weeks later. However, it was possible to change your courses within the first week of the semester if there were available spots for the courses. Be aware that it is your own responsibility to choose courses, that do not have time clashes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to the student mobility office at the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing but I ended up getting all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything is easier to fix when you get to the university. The student mobility office is very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is the individual professor that decides how the course is runned. However the university has some rules about the grading system that all courses must live up to. The professors do not always like this, which mean nothing is streamlined. Everything is so unstructured and it is very hard to be a part of as a abroad student. Many of the professors do not use reading lists. It is mostly about remembering stuff rather than understanding the theory and processes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of classroom participation and midterms. They take attendance in most courses, and you can't take the exam if you don't come to class. They also do a lot of simulations and roleplayes which often counts for you final grade. Almost every test is closed book and they care more about if you can remeber the correct names rather than understanding and using the theories and models.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Industrial Policy in Europe, Sociology of Terrorism and Political Violence, History of Foreign Italian Policy, Crisis Communication, Security Law and Constitutional Protection.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Industrial Policy in Europe. This was the only good course I had. It was exciting, the professors were skilled and passionate, and they spoke understandable English.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot more on food than I expected. I also spend a lot more on eating out as it was a big part of the culture

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many social and cultural activities available. The Erasmus group of the University had plans you could attend more days every week. It was very good and there were so many exchange students to do all the fun stuff with.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The football tournament, all the fun parties that the Erasmus Team plans. I would really recommend to by the intro package through Erasmus. It is a bit expensive but totally worth it in terms of getting to know people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All the cultural sights in Rome. I also recommend to use the fast trains in Italy to go on weekend trips to other cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time to get use to the new culture but it was a fun experience.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The way they act so rude in public transportation.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How they live life more slowly. There going-out culture. The streets were always filled with people enjoying a drink in the evening. There very delicious food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1)Get used to the university being very unstructured. If you can try to find some locals students, who can help you understand the system. 2) Say yes to all the social events in the beginning, it is so much fun. 3) Find housing in walking distance from Campus if possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remeber you can change courses the first week of the semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural and social experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To understand the university teaching system.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
